page.title: IT Company Simulator
page.eyebrow: VARIATOR · IT services company · one year
page.lead: An IT services company (12M USD ARR, 20 people) plans the next year. Which lever gives the best year: status quo, pay down technical debt, hire 5 engineers, reserve GPU capacity, or raise prices by 8%? The model links finance, clients, product, operations, people, market and external risks.
page.scope: 🏢 Company level (strategy). This page compares levers for the whole company over one year. To choose how to deliver one project or release (in-house, nearshore or offshore), use the case Best way to deliver.
change: Your preference: weights of cash, runway, churn, SLA and NPS; risk aversion.
Any factor of the 7 blocks: a fixed value or a range (low, likely, high).
Shocks: the probability and the size of each event (GPU shortage, vendor prices, FX, regulation, competitor, key person, key account, reputation, macro).
Links: each k coefficient sets how strongly one factor moves the next one.
Levers of each option (for example the price change).
real: Each block has a real data source: finance, CRM, PMO, monitoring, incident tool, CI/CD, HR, cloud bills, market reports.
The numbers here are a plausible example company, not real data. Put in your own numbers to model your company.
The chains matter more than the list: a GPU shortage raises infra cost and latency, the SLA falls, churn rises, revenue and cash fall.
The k coefficients are assumptions. Calibrate them with your history (for example churn after past SLA breaches).
metrics: Outputs: cash at year end, runway (months), churn, SLA (availability), NPS; score, P(best), feasible share, RAG. Runway has fixed RAG limits: green from 18 months, red at 6 months or less.
Chain values: capacity, infra cost, latency, incidents, time to restore, SLA, overdue, NPS, churn, roadmap, new ARR, CAC spend, revenue, cost, burn, runway, gross margin, LTV/CAC.
Rules: burnout (a team load after the hires above 1.05 adds 5 points of attrition), runway below 6 months fails, SLA and churn flags, budget flag. The limits are inputs under “Limits and thresholds”.
Not modelled yet: month-by-month dynamics, several products, sales seasonality.

risks.cash: 💰 You may need a credit line or cost cuts by year end

section.stays.title: As before
section.stays.body: Inputs that no fork changes. The inputs with a metric at T start from the history (the company facts): ARR, cash, receivables days, team load and deploys as measured; time to restore, incidents, latency, support quality (from the NPS) and the base churn so that the plan without shocks gives the measured values. Every other input, the k links and the limits are model assumptions. The forecast differs from T: the shocks, the uncertainty and the links act over the year.
section.stays.more: The common ground of all options: the values that no fork, hypothesis or event changes. Correct them only when the data is wrong.

section.month-answer.title: Answer
section.month-answer.body: The fork with the best score times the share of feasible scenarios. The sentence says what you aim for, what to choose and when to look again. The cards show the median and the 5%-95% range of each criterion; the risks come as consequences with their odds.
section.month-answer.more: The best fork in one sentence, its expected result and the three main risks.

section.month-compare.title: Compare
section.month-compare.body: Each criterion is scaled 0-1 across the forks, weighted and summed. The order uses score x feasible share. Change the priorities or the caution level: the ranking changes at once, without a new simulation.
section.month-compare.more: Ranking, criteria per fork and your priorities; a priority change reranks at once.

section.month-time.title: Over time
section.month-time.body: A preview: monthly paths drawn to end at the year-end results of the model. The fan shows the median and the 25-75% and 10-90% ranges. section.month-time.more: Monthly fans per fork and the risk calendar: when cash, runway, SLA, churn, cost or a milestone can fail.

section.month-details.body: For the analyst: the spread of each criterion per fork (box plots), the RAG shares with their limits, histograms, and the number of scenarios and the seed of the run.
section.month-details.more: Outputs: cash at year end, runway (months), churn, SLA (availability), NPS; score, P(best), feasible share, RAG. Runway has fixed RAG limits: green from 18 months, red at 6 months or less. Chain values: capacity, infra cost, latency, incidents, time to restore, SLA, overdue, NPS, churn, roadmap, new ARR, CAC spend, revenue, cost, burn, runway, gross margin, LTV/CAC. Rules: burnout (a team load after the hires above 1.05 adds 5 points of attrition), runway below 6 months fails, SLA and churn flags, budget flag. The limits are inputs under “Limits and thresholds”. Not modelled yet: month-by-month dynamics, several products, sales seasonality.

section.week-review.title: Review
section.week-review.body: Choose the forks for the week and day steps. A fork whose range of results overlaps the leader is marked: better keep it, it can still win.
section.week-review.more: Keep the forks worth a closer look; a fork whose range overlaps the leader is marked.

section.week.title: Paths
section.week.body: A preview: weekly paths as a tree. Each node gives 3 variants of the next week; each level keeps at most 60 nodes, so the tree stays a fair sample. A thicker branch carries more paths.
section.week.more: Pick a fork and see how its year can go, week by week: the common paths, the bad branches to watch, and how far the numbers can spread.

section.day-review.title: Review
section.day-review.body: The day level shows three example scenarios of each fork you pick: pessimistic, median and optimistic. Pick one or two forks.
section.day-review.more: Pick one or two forks for the example days.

section.day.title: Examples
section.day.body: A preview: three example scenarios of a fork, from the bad, the typical and the good part of the scenarios. Each shows daily cash, team load and incidents for the first 60 working days, and the events.
section.day.more: Three example scenarios (bad, typical, good): daily cash, load, incidents and events.

step.forks.title: Forks
step.forks.body: Step 1: choose what to compare. Changes here make the later steps out of date until they run again.

step.month.title: Month
step.month.body: Step 2: the horizon as a Monte Carlo of the cause-and-effect model, per fork.

step.week.title: Week
step.week.body: Step 3: weekly paths for the forks you choose in the review card.

kpi.decision.title: Decision
kpi.decision.body: The fork with the highest score x feasible share at your priorities.

kpi.strategy.title: Strategy
kpi.strategy.body: What you aim for, what to choose, and when to examine the choice again, in 1-2 sentences.

kpi.score.title: Score
kpi.score.body: Each criterion scaled 0-1 on fixed anchors (the 1st to 99th percentile of the baseline fork), times its weight, summed. A change of one fork changes only its own score. A gap to the baseline counts only beyond the meaningful difference of the criterion (inputs under Limits and thresholds).

kpi.pBest.title: P(best)
kpi.pBest.body: Share of scenarios where the fork has the highest weighted score of all the forks compared (the same fixed anchors as the score). The label beside it says how many forks that is («of 5 forks»): the review before the week or the day lists only some forks, but each one's P(best) is still out of all of them. Two forks equal on every criterion share the scenarios they win, so the verdict gives them together («together best in»). Failed scenarios do not count for it. In each scenario, gaps below the meaningful difference of a criterion are ties.

kpi.feasible.title: Feasible
kpi.feasible.body: Share of scenarios where no check rule fails (for example: runway below 6 months).

kpi.overallRag.title: Overall RAG
kpi.overallRag.body: Per scenario, the worst colour over the weighted criteria: green, amber or red.

kpi.limits.title: RAG limits
kpi.limits.body: Runway has fixed limits: green from 18 months, red at 6 months or less (inputs under Limits and thresholds). The other criteria take them from the baseline fork (keep the plan): green = its median; red = its worst 10%. Flags make a colour worse; a failed check makes it red.

kpi.expected.title: Expected result
kpi.expected.body: Median and the range of 90% of the outcomes (5% to 95%) of each criterion for the chosen fork.

kpi.breaks.title: Changes if
kpi.breaks.body: Single changes after which another fork leads clearly (by more than 0.02 of score): one weight halved or doubled, or another caution level.

kpi.risks.title: Risks to watch
kpi.risks.body: Consequences for you, most important first: the odds in words, a fork that makes it less likely, and the input to watch.

kpi.odds.title: Odds
kpi.odds.body: The share of scenarios in words: 3 in 10, 1 in 12, below 1 in 50.

kpi.watch.title: What to watch
kpi.watch.body: The input whose values correlate most with the bad outcome (|r| at least 0.1).

kpi.tradeoff.title: Trade-off
kpi.tradeoff.body: On which criteria the leader is better than the second fork (and by how much on average), the reverse, and where the two are equal within the meaningful difference.

kpi.vsBase.title: Compared with the base
kpi.vsBase.body: The difference to the run without your changes: up = better, down = worse.

kpi.pMet.title: P(met)
kpi.pMet.body: Share of scenarios where the milestone or goal is met by its date. Target: 80%.

kpi.forecastBand.title: Forecast
kpi.forecastBand.body: In 80% of the scenarios the milestone is reached in this range of months; the line is the median month. Your date does not change the forecast.

kpi.spare.title: Months spare
kpi.spare.body: Your date minus the month that 8 of 10 scenarios meet: positive = spare time, negative = more time needed.

kpi.conflicts.title: Inputs in conflict
kpi.conflicts.body: For a missed goal, the random inputs that correlate most with the miss (C1-C3). Too high or too low gives the direction.

kpi.plan.title: Plan
kpi.plan.body: Levers of the fork in order (what, how much, when). Each takes the value with the most goals met, then the latest start.

kpi.chainValue.title: Chain value
kpi.chainValue.body: The mean of a link of the cause-and-effect chain over all scenarios, per fork.

kpi.drivers.title: Main drivers
kpi.drivers.body: Inputs that move cash most for this fork.
kpi.drivers.more: The correlation of each uncertain input with cash at year end over the scenarios. A bar to the right: higher values give more cash; to the left: they cost cash.

kpi.range.title: Range
kpi.range.body: Low, likely and high value of an uncertain input.
kpi.range.more: Each scenario draws a value from this range. Most draws fall near the likely value; the curve shows the shape (a PERT distribution).

kpi.ruleShare.title: Rule share
kpi.ruleShare.body: Share of scenarios where the rule fired, per fork.

kpi.boxplot.title: Box plot
kpi.boxplot.body: Box = middle 50% of the scenarios; whiskers = the range of the slider; thick line = median; dot = mean; dashed lines = RAG limits.

kpi.ragTable.title: RAG detail
kpi.ragTable.body: Per criterion and fork, the share of green, amber and red scenarios.

kpi.histogram.title: Histogram
kpi.histogram.body: How often each value occurs, one line per fork; dashed lines are the RAG limits.

kpi.runMeta.title: Run
kpi.runMeta.body: Number of scenarios, the seed and the time of the last simulation. The same seed gives the same result.

kpi.fan.title: Fan
kpi.fan.body: Median line; the dark band holds 50% of the paths (25-75%), the light band 80% (10-90%). Preview data.

kpi.riskCalendar.title: Risk calendar
kpi.riskCalendar.body: Chance that the check, limit, milestone or goal has failed by each month (cumulative). Preview data.

kpi.medianFirstMonth.title: Typical month
kpi.medianFirstMonth.body: Among the scenarios where it fails, the median month of the first failure.

kpi.weekTree.title: Week tree
kpi.weekTree.body: Weeks on the axis; a branch is a group of paths; a thicker branch carries more paths. Click a node for the week summary. Preview data.

kpi.weekNode.title: Week node
kpi.weekNode.body: One week of one group of paths: cash, team load and incidents, and a short summary.

kpi.dayExample.title: Example future
kpi.dayExample.body: A scenario of the model from the bad (10%), typical (50%) or good (90%) part of cash at year end. Preview data.

kpi.dayEvents.title: Events
kpi.dayEvents.body: What happens on each day of the example: incidents, payments, shocks and decisions. A link opens the record in the knowledge base.

kpi.simulationBadge.title: Simulation
kpi.simulationBadge.body: These numbers are a simulated future, not recorded data.

kpi.preview.title: Preview
kpi.preview.body: Stand-in data drawn to match the model at the horizon, until the month-by-month simulation on actors is ready.

kpi.stale.title: Out of date
kpi.stale.body: An input changed after this result. It updates after the next run.

control.hypotheses.title: World hypotheses
control.hypotheses.body: Typical situations as layers. Turn on one or more: they add up in a fixed order. Your own edits stay on top.

control.priorityPresets.title: Priorities
control.priorityPresets.body: Ready weight sets. Balanced = the model defaults. A preset sets all weights; you can then move each one.

control.weights.title: Weights
control.weights.body: How much each criterion counts in the score, 0-3. Only the ratios matter.

control.caution.title: How careful?
control.caution.body: On average = rank by the mean; with a margin = a quarter of the weight on the worst 5%; worst 5% = rank by the bad cases only.

control.compare.title: Compare with the start
control.compare.body: Shows the difference to a run without your changes and hypotheses.

control.timelineOption.title: Show for
control.timelineOption.body: The fork whose timeline, conflicts and plan are shown; default: the best fork.

control.eventButtons.title: Events
control.eventButtons.body: Place a certain event (GPU shortage, supplier price rise, key account or key engineer leaves) on the timeline, then move it to its month.

control.dragMarker.title: Move a date
control.dragMarker.body: Drag a marker, or focus it and press the arrow keys (half a month; Shift: a month). Esc during a drag moves it back.

control.suggestDates.title: Suggest dates
control.suggestDates.body: Each milestone moves to the month that 8 of 10 scenarios meet, rounded up to half a month.

control.applyPlan.title: Apply the plan
control.applyPlan.body: Sets the levers of the plan (the start months) on the timeline.

control.deleteItem.title: Delete
control.deleteItem.body: Removes the milestone or goal from the evaluation. Restore it from the list.

control.restoreItem.title: Restore
control.restoreItem.body: Brings a deleted milestone or goal back.

control.resetField.title: Back to the default
control.resetField.body: Removes your edit of this value; a hypothesis value stays.

control.resetSection.title: Reset the section
control.resetSection.body: Removes your changes in this section only.

control.resetAll.title: Back to the start
control.resetAll.body: Removes all your changes and hypotheses. You can undo it in the notification.

control.undo.title: Undo
control.undo.body: Restores the value before this change.

control.modelSettings.title: Model settings
control.modelSettings.body: All inputs by block, the link coefficients, the shocks and the levers. A changed value has a dot; a hypothesis value has a mark.

control.inspector.title: Intervention
control.inspector.body: The value and its range (low, likely, high) of the selected intervention, its source, its owner and what it changes.

control.n.title: Scenarios
control.n.body: Number of simulated scenarios. More gives smoother numbers and takes longer.

control.seed.title: Seed
control.seed.body: Start of the random numbers. The same seed gives the same result.

control.whiskers.title: Whiskers
control.whiskers.body: The range of the box-plot whiskers, from 1%-99% to 25%-75%.

control.forkSelection.title: Forks for the next steps
control.forkSelection.body: Choose the forks for the week and day steps. A fork whose range overlaps the leader is marked: better keep it.

control.dayForks.title: Forks for the day level
control.dayForks.body: Pick one or two forks to see day by day.
control.dayForks.more: The day level shows three example scenarios of each fork you pick: pessimistic, median and optimistic.

control.exampleChoice.title: Example future
control.exampleChoice.body: Choose the pessimistic, the median or the optimistic example.
control.exampleChoice.more: The examples are scenarios of the model from the bad (10%), the typical (50%) and the good (90%) part of the first criterion.

control.openInKb.title: Open in the knowledge base
control.openInKb.body: Shows the brief, dossiers and questions on this example branch, marked as a simulation.

recompute.baseline.title: Baseline
recompute.baseline.body: The fork every delta is measured against.
recompute.baseline.more: The baseline is always compared, and every vs-baseline delta on the page is measured against it. Its RAG limits are the green and red lines of the other forks.

recompute.overlay.title: Overlay
recompute.overlay.body: Recomputed as an overlay on the same paths: instant.
recompute.overlay.more: An overlay fork changes only prices or values on top of the same scenario paths; no actor reacts to the change by itself. The recompute is instant.

recompute.from_date.title: Rerun from its date
recompute.from_date.body: The paths are rerun from the start date of the fork.
recompute.from_date.more: This fork changes how the company works from its start month. The scenarios are rerun from that month on; earlier months stay the same.

recompute.structural.title: Structural
recompute.structural.body: New actors or rules: the whole horizon is rerun.
recompute.structural.more: This fork adds something new to the company or the project, for example a second cloud or a vendor team. The whole horizon is rerun, and the ranges are wider.

lane.decisions.title: Decisions
lane.decisions.body: What you decide and when it starts: the levers of the forks.

lane.people.title: People
lane.people.body: Events about people: a key engineer leaves, a hire starts later.

lane.clients_vendors.title: Clients and vendors
lane.clients_vendors.body: Events at clients and suppliers: a client gives notice, a vendor raises prices or rotates its team.

lane.factors.title: Factors
lane.factors.body: Outside factors: shortages, markets, currency and regulation.

criterion.cash.title: Cash at year end
criterion.cash.body: Cash at the end of the year, USD; higher is better. Default weight 1.
criterion.cash.more: You may need a credit line or cost cuts by year end

criterion.runway.title: Runway
criterion.runway.body: Months of cash at the end of the year, months; higher is better. Default weight 0.5.
criterion.runway.more: You get less time to react: fundraising or cuts come sooner

criterion.churn.title: Client churn
criterion.churn.body: Annual client churn, share; lower is better. Default weight 1.
criterion.churn.more: You lose more clients and their recurring revenue

criterion.sla.title: Availability (SLA)
criterion.sla.body: Availability, share; higher is better. Default weight 0.75.
criterion.sla.more: SLA penalties and angry clients are possible

criterion.nps.title: NPS
criterion.nps.body: Net promoter score, points; higher is better. Default weight 0.5.
criterion.nps.more: Fewer referrals and renewals; churn can grow

fork.pay_tech_debt.title: Reduce tech debt
fork.pay_tech_debt.body: Use 15% of capacity for technical debt for a year.
fork.pay_tech_debt.more: Sets: Lever: 15% of capacity pays down technical debt = 1.

fork.hire_5.title: Hire 5 engineers
fork.hire_5.body: Hire 5 engineers (cost from the month they join).

fork.reserve_gpu.title: Reserve GPU capacity
fork.reserve_gpu.body: Reserve GPU capacity on a second cloud (+0.3M per year).
fork.reserve_gpu.more: Sets: Lever: reserved GPU capacity on a second cloud = 1.

hypothesis.price_war.title: Price war
hypothesis.price_war.body: The chance of a competitor price cut rises from 30% to 65%, and the cut is 1.5 times deeper.
hypothesis.price_war.more: A competitor cuts prices: chance 30% -> 65%; A competitor cuts prices: size x 1.5.

hypothesis.gpu_crunch.title: GPU shortage
hypothesis.gpu_crunch.body: The chance of a GPU shortage rises from 25% to 62%, and of a supplier price rise from 20% to 44%.
hypothesis.gpu_crunch.more: GPU shortage at the cloud provider: chance 25% -> 62%; NVIDIA, AWS or a supplier raises prices: chance 20% -> 44%.

hypothesis.big_client_leaves.title: Big client may leave
hypothesis.big_client_leaves.body: A key account gives notice with a much higher chance, and the account it takes is 1.5 times larger.
hypothesis.big_client_leaves.more: A key account leaves: chance 10% -> 64%; A key account leaves: size x 1.5.

hypothesis.client_requirements_churn.title: Clients change requirements
hypothesis.client_requirements_churn.body: Clients change requirements and priorities often: more blockers, higher load, more late implementations.
hypothesis.client_requirements_churn.more: Share of time lost to blockers: x 1.5; Planned work / capacity: x 1.08; Share of client implementations that are late: x 1.3.

hypothesis.hiring_freeze.title: Hard to hire
hypothesis.hiring_freeze.body: Hiring takes 4 months longer, and attrition is 20% higher.
hypothesis.hiring_freeze.more: Months to hire and onboard: + 4 months; Annual staff attrition: x 1.2.

hypothesis.cash_squeeze.title: Cash squeeze
hypothesis.cash_squeeze.body: Funding is late: 30% less cash at the start, and clients pay 30 days later.
hypothesis.cash_squeeze.more: Cash at the start: x 0.7; Receivables: days until clients pay: + 30 days.

hypothesis.downturn.title: Market downturn
hypothesis.downturn.body: The chance of a macro downturn rises from 20% to 60%, and demand growth is 5 points lower.
hypothesis.downturn.more: Macro downturn lowers demand: chance 20% -> 60%; Market demand growth: - 0.05 share.

hypothesis.payroll_tax_july.title: Payroll tax +5 pp from July
hypothesis.payroll_tax_july.body: A new employer payroll tax of 5 more points applies from July: the cost of the gross payroll rises by 5% for the rest of the year.
hypothesis.payroll_tax_july.more: Extra employer payroll tax on the gross payroll: + 0.05 share.

priority.balanced.title: Balanced
priority.balanced.body: The model defaults: cash and churn first, then availability, runway and NPS.

priority.cash_first.title: Cash first
priority.cash_first.body: Cash at year end and runway count most; clients and reliability count less.

priority.clients_first.title: Clients first
priority.clients_first.body: Client churn and NPS count most; cash counts less.

priority.reliability_first.title: Reliability first
priority.reliability_first.body: Availability (SLA) counts most, then churn; cash counts less.

caution.average.title: On average
caution.average.body: Rank by the mean result of all scenarios.

caution.margin.title: With a margin
caution.margin.body: Mostly the mean, with a quarter of the weight on the worst 5% (the default).

caution.worst.title: Worst 5%
caution.worst.body: Rank by the mean of the worst 5% of the scenarios only.

rule.burnout.title: Burnout raises attrition
rule.burnout.body: A team over capacity after the hires loses more people. An effect rule changes an input when its condition is true.
rule.burnout.formula: if load > burnout_load: attrition = attrition + burnout_attrition

rule.runway_low.title: Runway below 6 months
rule.runway_low.body: Less cash than for 6 months (the runway red limit) is not acceptable. A check rule: when it fails, the scenario is not acceptable (infeasible).
rule.runway_low.formula: if runway < runway_red: fail: Runway is below its red limit (6 months by default)

rule.sla_breach.title: SLA breach
rule.sla_breach.body: A flag rule sets a RAG colour on a criterion.
rule.sla_breach.formula:
if sla < sla_target: red on sla
elif sla < sla_target + 0.002: amber on sla

rule.over_budget.title: Cost above budget
rule.over_budget.body: Total cost above the annual budget. A flag rule sets a RAG colour on a criterion.
rule.over_budget.formula: if cost > budget: amber on cash

rule.churn_high.title: High churn
rule.churn_high.body: A flag rule sets a RAG colour on a criterion.
rule.churn_high.formula:
if churn > g_churn: red on churn
elif churn > 0.75 * g_churn: amber on churn

derived.price_live.title: New prices live
derived.price_live.body: Month when the new prices apply, month. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.price_live.more: Inputs: Month when the new prices are announced, Contract notice before new prices apply. Used by: Price change over the year (from the month it applies).

derived.debt_ready.title: Month when the debt work shows an effect
derived.debt_ready.body: Month when the debt work shows an effect, month. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.debt_ready.more: Inputs: Months until the debt work shows an effect, Month when the technical-debt work starts. Used by: Technical debt after the debt lever.

derived.hire_ready.title: Month when the new hires join (their work and their cost start)
derived.hire_ready.body: Month when the new hires join (their work and their cost start), month. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.hire_ready.more: Inputs: Months to hire and onboard, Month when the hiring starts. Used by: Share of the year in which the new hires work.

derived.gpu_ready.title: GPU capacity ready
derived.gpu_ready.body: Month when the GPU capacity is ready, month. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.gpu_ready.more: Inputs: Months to set up the second cloud, Month when the GPU reservation is ordered. Used by: GPU shortage.

derived.price_eff.title: Price change over the year (from the month it applies)
derived.price_eff.body: Price change over the year (from the month it applies), share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.price_eff.more: Inputs: Lever: list price change, New prices live. Used by: Client churn, New ARR, Revenue.

derived.gpu_total.title: GPU shortage: shock events + a placed event (rest of the year)
derived.gpu_total.body: GPU shortage: shock events + a placed event (rest of the year), share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.gpu_total.more: Inputs: Placed event: a GPU shortage (1 = yes), Month of the GPU shortage, Size of the placed GPU shortage, GPU shortage severity. Used by: GPU shortage.
derived.gpu_total.formula: gpu_total = gpu_shortage + ev_gpu * ev_gpu_size * maximum(12 - ev_gpu_month, 0) / 12

derived.vendor_total.title: Supplier price rise: shock events + a placed event
derived.vendor_total.body: Supplier price rise: shock events + a placed event, share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.vendor_total.more: Inputs: Placed event: a supplier raises prices by 10% (1 = yes), Month of the supplier price rise, Price rise of the placed supplier event, Price rise by NVIDIA, AWS or another supplier. Used by: Infrastructure cost.
derived.vendor_total.formula: vendor_total = vendor_price + ev_vendor * ev_vendor_size * maximum(12 - ev_vendor_month, 0) / 12

derived.account_total.title: ARR lost with key accounts: shock events + a placed event
derived.account_total.body: ARR lost with key accounts: shock events + a placed event, share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.account_total.more: Inputs: Placed event: a key account (10% of ARR) leaves (1 = yes), Month when the key account leaves, Share of ARR the placed key account takes, Share of ARR lost with a key account. Used by: Client churn.
derived.account_total.formula: account_total = key_account_lost + ev_account * ev_account_size * maximum(12 - ev_account_month, 0) / 12

derived.kp_total.title: Key engineer gone: shock events + a placed event (share of the year)
derived.kp_total.body: Key engineer gone: shock events + a placed event (share of the year), share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.kp_total.more: Inputs: Placed event: a key engineer leaves (1 = yes), Month when the key engineer leaves, A key engineer leaves (1 = yes). Used by: Delivery capacity, Time to restore.

derived.hire_effect.title: Share of the year in which the new hires work
derived.hire_effect.body: Share of the year in which the new hires work, share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.hire_effect.more: Inputs: Month when the new hires join (their work and their cost start), Lever: hire 5 engineers. Used by: Team load after the hires, Cost of the new hires in the year (from the month they join).

derived.debt_eff.title: Technical debt after the debt lever
derived.debt_eff.body: Technical debt after the debt lever, index. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.debt_eff.more: Inputs: Month when the debt work shows an effect, Lever: 15% of capacity pays down technical debt, Technical debt index (0 = none, 1 = severe). Used by: Latency, Incidents, Late implementations.

derived.load.title: Team load after the hires
derived.load.body: Team load after the hires, ratio. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.load.more: Inputs: Staff at the start of the year, Engineers the hiring lever hires, Share of the year in which the new hires work, Planned work / capacity. Used by: Delivery capacity, Incidents.

derived.hire_cost.title: Cost of the new hires in the year (from the month they join)
derived.hire_cost.body: Cost of the new hires in the year (from the month they join), USD/year. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.hire_cost.more: Inputs: Annual cost of one new engineer (salary, tax and overhead), Engineers the hiring lever hires, Share of the year in which the new hires work. Used by: Cost, Delivery payroll: the delivery share of the operating cost and the new hires.

derived.capacity.title: Delivery capacity
derived.capacity.body: Delivery capacity (1 = normal), ratio. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.capacity.more: Inputs: Annual staff attrition, Share of time lost to blockers, Share of delivery capacity the debt work takes, Key engineer gone: shock events + a placed event (share of the year), Lever: 15% of capacity pays down technical debt, Team load after the hires, Month when the technical-debt work starts, Productivity gain from new tools (for example AI assistants), Team skills index (1 = normal). Used by: Late implementations, Roadmap done.
derived.capacity.formula: capacity = (1 - debt_share * lever_debt * maximum(12 - m_debt, 0) / 12) * (1 - 0.5 * attrition) * (1 - 0.15 * kp_total) * (1 - blockers) * skills * (1 + new_tech_gain) / load

derived.gpu_hit.title: GPU shortage
derived.gpu_hit.body: GPU shortage after the GPU lever, share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.gpu_hit.more: Inputs: GPU capacity ready, GPU shortage: shock events + a placed event (rest of the year), Lever: reserved GPU capacity on a second cloud. Used by: Infrastructure cost, Latency.

derived.infra_cost.title: Infrastructure cost
derived.infra_cost.body: Infrastructure cost, USD/year. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.infra_cost.more: Inputs: Cost increase from currency moves, GPU shortage, Annual cost of the reserved GPU capacity, Annual infrastructure and GPU cost, Infra cost growth per unit of GPU shortage, Lever: reserved GPU capacity on a second cloud, Month when the GPU reservation is ordered, Supplier price rise: shock events + a placed event. Used by: Cost, Gross margin after the infrastructure and the delivery payroll.
derived.infra_cost.formula: infra_cost = infra_base * (1 + k_infra_gpu * gpu_hit) * (1 + vendor_total) * (1 + fx_shock) + gpu_reserve_cost * lever_gpu * maximum(12 - m_gpu, 0) / 12

derived.latency.title: Latency
derived.latency.body: p95 latency, ms. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.latency.more: Inputs: Technical debt after the debt lever, GPU shortage, Latency growth per unit of technical debt, Latency growth per unit of GPU shortage, p95 API latency. Used by: Availability (SLA).
derived.latency.formula: latency = latency_base * (1 + k_lat_gpu * gpu_hit) * (1 + k_lat_debt * debt_eff)

derived.incidents.title: Incidents
derived.incidents.body: Incidents per month, count. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.

derived.nps.title: NPS
derived.nps.body: Net promoter score, points. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.nps.more: Inputs: Late implementations, Availability (SLA), Availability promised in the SLA, Support quality score (0-1). Used by: Client churn, criterion nps.

derived.churn.title: Client churn
derived.churn.body: Annual churn, share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.churn.more: Inputs: ARR lost with key accounts: shock events + a placed event, Annual churn without the effects below, Competitor price cut, Churn added per unit of competitor price cut, Churn added per NPS point below 30, on the renewal share, Churn added per unit of overdue implementations, Churn added per unit of price increase, Churn added per 0.1 pp of availability below the SLA, NPS, Late implementations, Price change over the year (from the month it applies), Share of ARR with a renewal this year, Extra churn from a reputation event, Availability (SLA), Availability promised in the SLA, Support quality score (0-1). Used by: Revenue, LTV / CAC, criterion churn.
derived.churn.formula: churn = clip(base_churn + k_churn_sla * maximum(sla_target - sla, 0) * 1000 + k_churn_overdue * overdue + k_churn_nps * renewal_due * maximum(30 - nps, 0) + k_churn_price * price_eff + k_churn_competitor * competitor_cut + account_total + reputation_hit - 0.1 * (support_quality - 0.8), 0, 0.9)

derived.roadmap.title: Roadmap done
derived.roadmap.body: Share of the roadmap delivered, share. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.
derived.roadmap.more: Inputs: Delivery capacity. Used by: New ARR.

derived.new_arr.title: New ARR
derived.new_arr.body: New ARR closed in the year, USD/year. A link of the cause-and-effect chain.

Used by: Acquisition spend for the new clients, Revenue.
derived.new_arr.formula: new_arr = pipeline * win_rate * (1 - k_win_price * price_eff) * (1 - competitor_cut) * (1 + demand_growth) * (0.8 + 0.2 * roadmap)

labels.arr0: Annual recurring revenue at the start

labels.win_rate: Share of the pipeline that closes

labels.blockers: Share of time lost to blockers
labels.new_tech_gain: Productivity gain from new tools (for example AI assistants)

labels.debt_share: Share of delivery capacity the debt work takes

labels.reputation_hit: Extra churn from a reputation event
labels.k_infra_gpu: Infra cost growth per unit of GPU shortage
labels.k_lat_gpu: Latency growth per unit of GPU shortage
labels.k_lat_debt: Latency growth per unit of technical debt
labels.k_inc_debt: Incident growth per unit of technical debt
labels.k_mttr_deploy: Elasticity of restore time to deploy frequency
labels.k_churn_sla: Churn added per 0.1 pp of availability below the SLA
labels.k_churn_overdue: Churn added per unit of overdue implementations
labels.k_churn_nps: Churn added per NPS point below 30, on the renewal share
labels.k_churn_price: Churn added per unit of price increase
labels.k_churn_competitor: Churn added per unit of competitor price cut
labels.k_win_price: Win-rate loss per unit of price increase
labels.m_price: Month when the new prices are announced

labels.ev_account: Placed event: a key account (10% of ARR) leaves (1 = yes)

labels.ms_hire: Milestone: the new hires are productive
